episode.title: Honor the telemetry payload-consent flag across diagnostic logging paths
episode.before: At parent commit dce13019b9e43b253d03e7fb2c12550cdd94e0aa, ordinary telemetry records emitted request_text, response_text, tool function_args, and complete tool metadata without consulting getTelemetryLogPromptsEnabled(). Policy-generation and verdict diagnostics likewise sent prompts, trusted content, generated policy, tool-call text, and verdict rationale through both OpenTelemetry and Clearcut regardless of that flag, although some semantic GenAI payload logging was already gated separately.
episode.after: At commit 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e, payload-bearing request, response, tool-call, policy-generation, and verdict attributes are added only when getTelemetryLogPromptsEnabled() is true. With the flag false, tool metadata is reduced to an explicit allowlist of aggregate line/character counters, while operational fields such as function name, verdict result, and errors remain available. The policy diagnostics apply the same rule to both OpenTelemetry and Clearcut.
episode.diff: The change modifies four telemetry files (437 insertions and 57 deletions): event serialization in types.ts now conditionally emits request_text, response_text, function_args, policy inputs/outputs, tool-call text, and rationale; tool metadata is filtered through eight explicitly safe aggregate keys and JSON-serialized; conseca-logger.ts conditionally constructs Clearcut sensitive-field entries while retaining verdict and error entries; tests add enabled/disabled assertions for API response text, API request text, tool arguments, and policy-generation/verdict fields across OpenTelemetry and Clearcut.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e is titled “Respect logPrompts flag for logging sensitive fields (#26153)”, has parent dce13019b9e43b253d03e7fb2c12550cdd94e0aa, and changes four telemetry implementation/test files.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, and changed_files_name_status

evidence_units.claim: In the parent, ToolCallEvent always placed serialized function_args and complete metadata in OpenTelemetry attributes; ApiRequestEvent always placed request_text there; ApiResponseEvent included response_text whenever present.
evidence_units.source: git show dce13019b9e43b253d03e7fb2c12550cdd94e0aa:packages/core/src/telemetry/types.ts, ToolCallEvent.toOpenTelemetryAttributes, ApiRequestEvent.toLogRecord, and ApiResponseEvent.toLogRecord

evidence_units.claim: In the parent, policy-generation OpenTelemetry attributes always included user_prompt, trusted_content, and policy, while verdict attributes always included user_prompt, policy, tool_call, verdict, and verdict_rationale.

The implementation gates tool arguments, API request text, API response text, policy-generation payloads, and verdict payloads on config.getTelemetryLogPromptsEnabled(), while leaving non-payload event attributes outside the conditional blocks.

When prompt logging is disabled, ToolCallEvent filters metadata to eight aggregate model/user added-or-removed line/character counters; when enabled it preserves all metadata, and it emits metadata only when the resulting object is nonempty.

The general telemetry logger passes Config into event record serializers, making the runtime prompt-logging preference available at the final OpenTelemetry attribute-construction boundary used by API and tool-call logging.
evidence_units.source: git show 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e:packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.ts; logApiRequest, logApiResponse, and logToolCall calls to event record/attribute serializers, corroborated by packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts

evidence_units.claim: The policy diagnostic logger now builds Clearcut data conditionally: payload entries are appended only when prompt logging is enabled, while verdict result and error entries remain unconditional; OpenTelemetry uses the correspondingly gated event serializers.
Logger tests assert that request_text and response_text are absent when prompt logging is disabled, and that response_text is present when it is enabled.
evidence_units.source: git show 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e:packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts, API request semantic-log disabled case and logApiResponse logPrompts cases

evidence_units.claim: Tool-call tests assert that function_args is absent while function_name remains when prompt logging is disabled, and that serialized function_args is present when the flag is enabled.

Policy diagnostic tests assert disabled-mode omission of user prompt, trusted content, policy, tool call, and rationale from OpenTelemetry and Clearcut, retention of verdict/error fields, and enabled-mode inclusion of sensitive fields.
evidence_units.source: git show 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e:packages/core/src/telemetry/conseca-logger.test.ts, added logPrompts enabled/disabled cases

evidence_units.claim: The added tests exercise both consent states and verify selective retention rather than disabling whole events: event name, function name, verdict result, and errors remain observable while payload fields are omitted.
The evidence bundle identifies PR/issue 26153 as a verified implementation-plus-test training candidate but reports that the issue body, discussion, reviews, and status checks are unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: gate-diagnostic-payload-fields
candidate_atomics.title: Gate diagnostic payload fields on explicit logging consent
candidate_atomics.description: At the final event-serialization boundary, omit free-form request, response, prompt, policy, tool-argument, tool-call, and rationale fields unless payload logging is explicitly enabled, while preserving non-payload operational attributes.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent user or model content from entering diagnostic records when payload logging has been disabled without suppressing the entire operational event.
semantic_action.pre_state: A diagnostic event contains free-form payload fields, and its serializer can access a runtime setting that expresses whether such payloads may be logged.
semantic_action.post_state: Payload fields are absent when consent is disabled and present when enabled; non-payload event identity, status, timing, and routing fields remain independently observable.
semantic_action.validation: Serialize representative API and tool events under both flag values; assert payload-key absence in disabled mode, payload-key presence in enabled mode, and retention of non-payload keys such as event name or function name.

candidate_atomics.name: allowlist-safe-aggregate-metadata
candidate_atomics.title: Reduce mixed diagnostic metadata to explicitly safe aggregates
candidate_atomics.description: When a metadata container can mix content-bearing values with harmless counters, retain only a small explicit allowlist of aggregate measurements while payload logging is disabled.

semantic_action.intent: Keep useful quantitative diagnostics without leaking arbitrary nested metadata that may contain user-derived content.
semantic_action.pre_state: A diagnostic metadata map may contain both approved aggregate counters and arbitrary or content-bearing keys, and payload logging is disabled.
semantic_action.post_state: Only explicitly approved aggregate keys remain; an empty sanitized map is not emitted, while enabled mode preserves the original metadata map.
semantic_action.validation: Serialize a metadata map containing approved counters and an unapproved nested value under disabled mode and assert that only approved keys remain; repeat under enabled mode and assert that the full map is preserved.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-redaction-across-telemetry-sinks
candidate_atomics.title: Apply the same payload boundary across telemetry sinks
candidate_atomics.description: Enforce the same consent decision in each backend-specific representation while retaining safe verdict and error diagnostics.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid a privacy bypass in which one diagnostic backend redacts sensitive fields but another backend still transmits them.
semantic_action.pre_state: One logical event is emitted to multiple telemetry sinks whose payloads are constructed through separate code paths.
semantic_action.post_state: Every sink omits the same sensitive payload categories when consent is disabled, while safe outcome and error fields continue to be emitted.
semantic_action.validation: Emit policy-generation and verdict events to each configured sink with the flag disabled and enabled; compare backend payloads for omission/inclusion and verify that verdict and error fields survive disabled mode.

candidate_workflows.name: enforce-consent-aware-diagnostic-redaction
candidate_workflows.title: Enforce consent-aware redaction at diagnostic emission boundaries
candidate_workflows.description: Identify content-bearing diagnostic fields, guard direct payload attributes, sanitize mixed metadata, reconcile all sink-specific encodings, and validate both privacy and retained observability.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure disabling payload logging removes sensitive or content-bearing values from every diagnostic representation while preserving useful non-sensitive operational telemetry.
when_to_use: A runtime privacy or consent flag is intended to control prompt, response, command, policy, rationale, or comparable free-form diagnostic payloads.
The same logical event is serialized through multiple record types or telemetry backends.
Structured metadata may combine safe aggregate measurements with arbitrary content-bearing values.
anti_goals: Do not disable all telemetry when only payload content requires suppression.
Do not remove safe event identity, timing, status, verdict, error, or aggregate measurement fields solely because payload logging is disabled.
Do not treat an entire extensible metadata object as safe merely because some of its current keys are numeric counters.
Do not change the meaning of the runtime consent flag or enable payload logging implicitly.
not_applicable_when: The diagnostic event contains no user-derived, model-derived, command, policy, rationale, or extensible metadata payload.
The system has no authoritative runtime control for payload logging and adding such a policy decision is outside the change scope.
The data must never be logged under any configuration; such fields require unconditional removal rather than consent-based gating.
inputs: Inventory of content-bearing fields for each event type
Inventory of non-sensitive operational fields that must remain observable
All backend-specific serializers and adapters for the affected events
Representative enabled-mode and disabled-mode test fixtures
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least one diagnostic serialization path emits content-bearing fields without consistently consulting the authoritative payload-logging setting.
workflow_graph.exit_state: For all affected events and sinks, disabled mode emits no identified payload fields, enabled mode preserves intentionally supported payloads, mixed metadata is limited to approved aggregates in disabled mode, and safe operational fields remain observable.

steps.condition: Apply to every direct diagnostic attribute classified as request, response, prompt, policy, command/tool argument, tool-call content, or explanatory rationale.
steps.validation: Enabled/disabled serialization tests prove omission and inclusion while also checking at least one retained operational field.

steps.condition: Apply when an extensible metadata object contains both approved aggregate diagnostics and potentially content-bearing keys.
steps.validation: A mixed-key metadata fixture proves that disabled mode emits only allowlisted aggregates and omits the container when no safe keys remain.

steps.condition: Apply whenever affected events have more than one sink-specific payload builder or serializer.
steps.validation: Backend-specific tests prove equivalent omission of sensitive categories and continued emission of safe verdict/error data.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent and patched serializers to confirm every identified direct payload field moved behind the runtime consent check.
Run unit cases with payload logging disabled and assert absence of request text, response text, tool arguments, prompts, policies, tool-call content, and rationale.
Run paired enabled-mode cases and assert intentionally supported payload fields remain available.
Verify non-sensitive event name, function name, verdict result, and error fields remain in disabled mode.
For mixed metadata, verify only the explicit aggregate allowlist survives disabled mode and arbitrary nested keys do not.
Exercise every backend-specific representation of the same logical event to detect sink-specific redaction bypasses.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if no authoritative runtime setting defines whether payload content may be logged.
Stop if the sensitive-field inventory or backend inventory cannot be established from implementation and call sites.
Do not declare completion if any affected sink still receives a classified payload in disabled mode.
Do not broaden the allowlist when a metadata key's safety cannot be established.
Stop and require an unconditional-removal decision if a field is prohibited even when payload logging is enabled.
unresolved_or_deferred: The changed tests do not include a dedicated disabled-mode mixed-metadata fixture proving that unapproved metadata keys are removed while approved aggregate counters remain.

The supplied GitHub bundle does not contain CI status checks or review discussion, and tests were not independently executed during extraction because the checkout worktree is fully deleted/dirty and some partial-clone objects require unavailable network access.

unresolved_questions: Were all repository test suites and status checks successful for commit 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e? The evidence bundle marks status checks unavailable.

Should a dedicated regression test be added for disabled-mode tool metadata containing both allowlisted aggregate counters and an unapproved nested payload? The implementation establishes this behavior, but the changed tests directly cover tool arguments rather than that negative metadata case.

The logger functions write complete event objects to debugLogger.debug before backend redaction. This commit does not change that path, and the available evidence does not establish whether debugLogger performs separate filtering or whether that local diagnostic path is in scope.
